messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure stems from how PosixParser handles an unrecognized short option when stopAtNonOption is enabled. In the failing test, args are ["-z", "-a", "-btoast"], and the expectation is that encountering the unrecognized "-z" should stop option parsing so that "-a" is not treated as an option.

Walking through PosixParser.flatten:
- The first token "-z" has length 2, so flatten delegates to processOptionToken("-z", true).
- In processOptionToken, when options.hasOption(token) is false and stopAtNonOption is true, it only sets eatTheRest = true (lines 238–241) and does not add any tokens, nor the end-of-options marker (“--”).
- After returning to flatten, gobble(iter) sees eatTheRest and appends the remaining tokens as-is (i.e., "-a", "-btoast") to the token list (lines 168–174).

Because processOptionToken did not add “--” nor the actual unrecognized token "-z", the unrecognized token is effectively dropped, and the subsequent tokens are still raw option-like tokens. The main Parser then interprets "-a" as a valid option, causing cl.hasOption("a") to be true, which fails the test’s assertion.

This matches the current bug report: “PosixParser doesn't handle properly unrecognized tokens starting with '-' when stopAtNonOption is enabled, the token is simply ignored.” The correct behavior (as implemented elsewhere in PosixParser, e.g., process(value) used by burstToken when encountering non-option content) is to emit “--” and the offending token so that all following tokens are treated as arguments. The omission occurs specifically in processOptionToken for 2-character tokens.

Root cause: In org.apache.commons.cli.PosixParser.processOptionToken(String, boolean), when stopAtNonOption is true and the token is not a recognized option, the method only sets eatTheRest and fails to add “--” and the token itself to the tokens list (i.e., it should behave like process(token) does).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
